newsitem.title: JAPAN: More Japan investment firms suspend Nomura deals.
newsitem.headline: More Japan investment firms suspend Nomura deals.

text.p: More Japanese investment management companies said on Monday that they had suspended business dealings with Nomura Securities Co Ltd in light of a scandal over suspected illegal deals.

Officials at Sakura Asset Management Co Ltd, Tokyo-Mitsubishi Asset Management Ltd and IBJ NW Asset Management Co Ltd confirmed that their companies had stopped giving Nomura any new orders as of Monday.

An official at Sakura Asset Management, a unit of Sakura Bank Ltd, said business with Nomura would be suspended for a while until Japan's securities watchdog, the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC), and the Finance Ministry come up with any necessary action against Nomura.
Meanwhile, a Sakura Bank spokesman said that the bank suspended business with Nomura on Monday but that no long-term decision had been made regarding its ties with Nomura.
"We are taking a close watch on moves by the SESC and MOF," a Sakura bank spokesman said.
An official at Tokyo-Mitsubishi Asset Management, a unit of Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi Ltd, also said orders would be suspended for the time being.
"We are suspending business with Nomura. We will decide what we should do (in the longer term) after official actions are decided upon," the official said.
An official at Nikko International Capital Management Co Ltd, an investment advisory unit of Nikko Securities Co Ltd, said the company had also suspended deals with Nomura.
He said that the suspension will last at least until the securities watchdog decides whether any punitive action against Nomura is necessary.
"We will suspend deals with Nomura until the SESC comes up a decision," the official said. He said his company would review its position after the outcome of the SESC probe.
He declined to give any estimate for the size of the transactions his company used to make with Nomura.

Nomura announced last week that two of its directors moved profits made on Nomura's own funds into a corporate client's account at their own discretion, a practice banned under Japan's securities law. Media reports have linked the firm with a former "sokaiya" racketeer but Nomura has said it cannot confirm such a link.
Earlier, Nomura group unit Nomura Investment Management Co Ltd said it was suspending its business with the brokerage from today following the news about the suspected illegal deals.
A company official said that orders given to Nomura Securities by Nomura Investment Management have accounted for about 20 percent of its total orders.
Daiwa International Capital Management Co Ltd, a unit of the Daiwa Securities Co Ltd group, also said it was halting its business with Nomura from Monday.
Neither company said how long the suspension would last.

Industry sources said that investment advisory firms are increasingly nervous about doing business with Nomura because their customers, including public funds such as pension funds, want asset management companies to suspend orders to Nomura.
The sources said foreign institutional investors, worried about the scandal, were also putting pressure on the companies to suspend dealings with Nomura, Japan's top securities house.

Meanwhile, stock market sources said that major life insurers were also considering suspending business with Nomura. An official at one major life insurance company said no decision had been made regarding business with Nomura.
